{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-5jpq","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-6mij.2.4: OSCORE authorize_mutating drops local_admin check for protected requests","description":"In commit 02a8ee28fd, the new coap_oscore_authorize_mutating() function replaces the old two-gate authorization pattern (OSCORE unprotect AND lichen_coap_is_local_admin) with an OR pattern: OSCORE auth OR local admin.

For keys_single_put (PUT /keys/{iid}), keys_single_delete (DELETE /keys/{iid}), deaddrop_post (POST /deaddrop), confessions_post (POST /confessions), and msg_inbox_post (POST /msg/inbox), this is a security downgrade.

OLD behavior: OSCORE-authenticated requests still had to pass lichen_coap_is_local_admin, which requires the peer to be on the local SLIP interface. This meant remote mesh peers with valid OSCORE contexts could NOT mutate keys or send deaddrop messages.

NEW behavior: An OSCORE-authenticated request from any mesh peer with a valid OSCORE context bypasses the local admin check entirely. This allows remote OSCORE-authenticated peers to PUT/DELETE keys, post to deaddrop/confessions, and post messages.

Fix options:
1. Add lichen_coap_is_local_admin check inside the OSCORE path of coap_oscore_authorize_mutating (restoring old behavior)
2. Remove the local admin check entirely for the non-OSCORE path too (aligning with the new intention)
3. Make the local admin check for non-OSCORE peers configurable per-resource

Files affected:
- lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/coap_oscore.c (lines 269-302)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_keys.c (lines 1018, 1100)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_dtn.c (lines 122, 233)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_server.c (lines 364)","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T15:59:00.00325486Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T15:59:00.00325486Z"}
